role.altitude: The midwife keeps examining, judging risk, talking with clients and deciding on referral; plotting measurements, chasing lab results, typing intake answers and writing contact notes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted notes and flags rather than writing and plotting by hand
role.ambitious_version: A midwife who spends the intake hour on the client's worries because the history is already in the record.

tasks.short: Measure and examine at check-ups, plot measurements against growth and blood pressure thresholds, identify and treat pregnancy-related problems or refer, write, sign and send the referral, and monitor follow-up.

steps.what: Midwife measures blood pressure and fundal height and asks about symptoms at check-ups
Midwife plots measurements on growth and blood pressure charts and compares them with guideline thresholds
Midwife identifies pregnancy-related problems and decides to treat, monitor or refer
Midwife writes the referral letter to the obstetrician
Midwife checks and signs the final referral letter
Midwife sends the signed referral to the hospital by secure mail
Midwife monitors follow-up: extra checks, glucose results and the obstetrician's reply

approvals.approved_version: the referral letter as signed by the midwife in s5; any change needs a new signature

tasks.design: Measurements entered during the check-up are plotted on growth and blood pressure charts in the midwifery record, and fixed guideline thresholds flag values that need attention. Identifying problems, treating and deciding on referral stay with the midwife. A referral template fills history and measurements from the record, the midwife writes the reason and signs, and sends it. Clients with a problem go on a follow-up list that shows overdue checks and results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts were plotted by hand and follow-ups tracked in memory or on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Midwifery records with growth charts, threshold flags and follow-up lists.
tasks.still_hard: Problems that show only as a client's feeling that something is wrong.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a normal number still needs a second look.
tasks.altitude: Less plotting and tracking; clinical judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether referrals arrive with complete charts.

evidence.claim: Software giving information used for diagnostic or therapeutic decisions is class IIa or higher.
The record is kept 20 years and includes signed drafts.
Growth charts and threshold flags in clinical records are fixed rules.

assumptions: Boundary: identifying and managing pregnancy problems in midwifery care; care after referral is outside.
Input contract for s2: measurements entered by the midwife during s1 and ultrasound biometry from the ultrasound centre's report; thresholds from the professional guideline set in the record.
Examination, decisions and sending keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether the practice's record software already plots charts.

incremental.description: Midwife reviews threshold settings when the guideline changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly healthy pregnancies; high: practices with many clients at risk.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have the client fill in the intake questionnaire, obtain complete health and medical histories in the intake conversation, request earlier records with consent, record the history and assess risk.

steps.what: Pregnant client fills in the intake questionnaire before the first visit
Midwife obtains medical, surgical, reproductive and mental health histories in the intake conversation
Midwife requests earlier records from the GP or hospital with the client's consent
Midwife records the complete history, checking the questionnaire answers already in the history fields
Midwife assesses risk against the indication list

tasks.design: The client fills in a structured intake questionnaire in the practice's patient portal before the first visit, and the answers land in the record's history fields. The midwife reads them before the intake and uses the conversation for what needs talking through, including mental health. Earlier records are requested through the regional care exchange with the client's consent. Risk assessment stays with the midwife.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every history question was asked and typed during the intake.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals with structured questionnaires feeding the record.
tasks.still_hard: Histories clients do not want to put on a form.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a client leaves out about violence or mental health.
tasks.altitude: Less typing at intake; the conversation stays.

reach.learn: Whether consent-based exchange replaces calls and letters.

evidence.claim: Health data are special category under the GDPR.
Midwives are BIG-registered and own their records.
Patient portals can feed questionnaire answers into structured record fields.

assumptions: Boundary: the intake history; later check-ups are outside.
Input contract for s4: questionnaire answers from clients through the portal, about 70% of clients; others answer in the conversation; s4 is priced at that share.
Clients' effort on the questionnaire is about what a paper intake form took and sits in s1.
The conversation keeps nearly full time.
unknowns: Share of clients who complete the questionnaire.
research_questions: Do intake conversations spend more time on mental health?

already_counted.description: Midwife checks questionnaire answers before the intake.

incremental.description: Midwife helps clients who cannot use the portal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many clients with language barriers who skip the questionnaire; high: most clients complete it.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect laboratory results and ultrasound reports, evaluate patients' laboratory and medical records, request assistance from other practitioners when necessary and inform the client.

steps.what: Midwife collects laboratory results and ultrasound reports from the lab and ultrasound centre
Midwife compares each value with its reference range, now marked when outside it
Midwife evaluates laboratory results and medical records
Midwife requests assistance from the obstetrician or GP when necessary
Midwife informs the client of the results and the plan

tasks.design: Lab results and ultrasound reports arrive as electronic messages in the client's record, matched to the order, instead of by mail, fax or portal look-ups. Values outside reference ranges are marked, and a list shows ordered tests still without a result. Evaluating, asking for help and informing the client stay with the midwife.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results came through several channels and were checked against orders by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic result messages from labs into midwifery records.
tasks.still_hard: Results that only make sense with the whole pregnancy in view.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a worrying result to an anxious client.

reach.learn: Whether midwives stop calling for missing results.

evidence.claim: Lab orders and results can flow between order systems and records without retyping.
Health data are special category under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating results and asking for help; treatment decisions after advice are separate.
Input contract for s1: result messages sent by the regional labs and ultrasound centres, about 80% of results; the rest arrive by mail and are attached by hand; s1 is priced at that share.
Evaluation, consultation and informing keep their full or nearly full time.

incremental.description: Midwife matches results that arrive without an order.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: labs still sending paper; high: all regional labs and centres sending electronic results.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write documentation of all patients' contacts, update the pregnancy record and care plan, review records before visits and handovers, and complete the registration for the perinatal registry.

steps.what: Midwife writes documentation of each contact: visits, calls and home visits

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the client's consent, and the record's note template.
loop.output: A draft contact note in the template's fields.
loop.check: The midwife reads and corrects every draft and signs it; no unsigned note enters the record; measurements must match those entered.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates alone still need the conversation typed.

steps.what: Midwife updates the pregnancy record: risk status and care plan
Midwife reviews records before visits and handovers to colleagues
Midwife completes the end-of-care registration for the perinatal registry

tasks.design: For consultations in the practice where the client agrees to recording, a certified scribe drafts the contact note into the record's template, and the midwife corrects and signs it. Calls and home visits are still typed. Updating the risk status and care plan stays with the midwife. Registry fields are filled as care happens from the structured record, and the record lists missing fields before the end-of-care registration.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after each contact and registry fields were completed at the end of care.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes that draft structured notes into clinical records, and registries fed from midwives' own software.
tasks.still_hard: Notes from home visits and births where recording does not fit.
tasks.human_edge: Recording what matters for the next colleague.
tasks.altitude: Less typing; the record stays the midwife's own.

evidence.claim: A scribe drafts structured consultation notes into clinical records and is NEN 7510 certified.
Midwives register in their own software, deliver the national dataset and compare their figures.
A summary tool that care plans build on is being certified as a class IIa medical device.
The record is kept 20 years and a signed AI draft is part of it.

assumptions: Boundary: documenting contacts and the registry delivery; analysis of registry figures is outside.
Input contract for s1: consultations in the practice recorded with the client's consent, about 60% of contacts; calls, home visits and births are typed; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s4: registry fields taken from the structured record kept by the midwife during care.
Updating the care plan keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of clients who consent to recording.
research_questions: Does note time per contact fall without errors rising?

already_counted.description: Midwife reads and corrects drafted notes.

incremental.description: Midwife asks for and records consent to recording.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: practices with many home visits and few recorded consults; high: busy practices with most consults recorded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
